name: High-salience LLM-associated vocabulary cluster
rationale: Several empirically overrepresented style markers in a short span are more informative than any one word.
revision: Replace the cluster with concrete verbs, measured claims, or domain terms. Keep any term that is technically exact.

name: Broad corpus-marker saturation
rationale: Common scientific words become informative only when many different corpus markers accumulate unusually densely.
revision: Retain necessary technical terms; revise only redundant or evaluative wording that displaces substance.

name: Evaluative adjective pile
rationale: Multiple praise or importance adjectives substitute evaluation for evidence.
revision: Delete self-evaluation and state the result, comparison, or criterion that earns the adjective.

name: Metaphorical abstraction cluster
rationale: Metaphors such as landscape, tapestry, realm, and journey can accumulate into faux conceptual depth.
revision: Name the actual system, population, process, or decision instead of stacking metaphors.

name: Importance-announcing meta-language
rationale: The sentence announces importance rather than establishing it.
revision: Delete the signpost and begin with the claim. Add evidence or a consequence where needed.

name: Section self-narration
rationale: Narrating document movement is often unnecessary in short scientific prose.
revision: Replace navigation with the substantive claim, except where a long technical paper genuinely needs a roadmap.

name: Generic era-framing opener
rationale: The opener supplies generic contemporaneity rather than a study-specific problem.
revision: Open with the population, unresolved estimate, mechanism, or decision that motivates the study.

name: Contribution boilerplate
rationale: A contribution claim is empty unless it states what changed relative to prior work.
revision: Specify the new estimand, dataset, comparison, mechanism, method, or contradiction.

name: Generic implications boilerplate
rationale: Generic impact language names no actor, decision, threshold, or action.
revision: State who should do what, for whom, under which conditions, and on the basis of which result.

name: Future-research boilerplate
rationale: A generic request for more research avoids specifying the unresolved identification or measurement problem.
revision: Name the missing population, comparison, mediator, time horizon, design, or source of uncertainty.

name: Generic conclusion formula
rationale: The conclusion repeats a significance template instead of carrying forward the study’s actual result.
revision: Conclude with the estimate, boundary condition, mechanism, or decision consequence.

name: Mechanical paragraph-transition repetition
rationale: Repeated stock transitions create a templated cadence and may conceal weak logical relations.
revision: Remove the transition where sentence order is sufficient; otherwise name the actual relation: contrast, mechanism, exception, or consequence.

name: Enumerative scaffolding
rationale: Enumeration is useful when the argument genuinely has ordered parts, but compulsive numbered scaffolds can substitute form for judgement.
revision: Keep the list only when each item is distinct, necessary, and ordered.

name: Triadic synonym list
rationale: Three near-synonyms often create the appearance of coverage without adding distinctions.
revision: Collapse synonyms or define how the three outcomes differ.

name: Unusually regular sentence length
rationale: Very low variation in sentence length can produce mechanical rhythm, but it is weak evidence by itself.
revision: Vary sentence structure only where argument structure benefits; do not manufacture variation.

name: Unusually regular paragraph length
rationale: Paragraphs of nearly identical length can signal template filling rather than idea-led development.
revision: Let paragraph length follow the claim and evidence rather than a visual template.

name: Nominalization density
rationale: Instruction-tuned models have shown higher nominalization rates, but nominalizations are also normal in scientific registers.
revision: Convert only unnecessary abstract nouns into verbs, especially where agency or causal sequence is obscured.

name: Sentence-initial participial-clause density
rationale: LLM prose can overuse sentence-initial present-participial clauses such as “Building on…” or “Highlighting…”.
revision: Check whether the participial clause has an explicit, unambiguous subject; rewrite when it creates a dangling modifier or repetitive cadence.

name: “That”-clause as sentence subject
rationale: Instruction-tuned LLMs have been reported to favor clauses beginning “That X …” as subjects.
revision: Revise only when the construction becomes repetitive or obscures the actor.

name: Noun-stack overload proxy
rationale: Long noun strings force readers to infer relationships among modifiers.
revision: Insert prepositions, verbs, or a short definition that states how the concepts relate.

name: Redundant hedge pair
rationale: Two uncertainty markers express one epistemic operation and dilute the claim.
revision: Retain the single hedge that best matches the design and uncertainty.

name: Hedge stack
rationale: Several distinct hedges in one short span make the degree and source of uncertainty unclear.
revision: State the claim once, then locate uncertainty in the estimate, design limitation, or explicit assumption.

name: Certainty inflation
rationale: Certainty is asserted rhetorically rather than tied to design, estimate, or sensitivity analysis.
revision: Replace the intensifier with the precise evidential claim and its boundary conditions.

name: Deontic or importance inflation
rationale: Normative force is asserted without specifying the decision consequence or opportunity cost.
revision: Name the decision, actor, expected benefit, trade-off, and evidential basis.

name: Unspecified consensus attribution
rationale: An unnamed consensus is not a source.
revision: Cite the relevant evidence or state the proposition directly with appropriate qualification.

name: False-balance scaffold
rationale: A symmetrical scaffold can imply evidential parity where none has been established.
revision: Compare the claims using explicit criteria: design strength, directness, precision, consistency, and relevance.

name: Result claim without numeric anchor
rationale: A Results sentence reports direction or significance but omits magnitude.
revision: Add the estimate, comparator, denominator where relevant, and uncertainty interval.

name: Effect estimate without uncertainty
rationale: A numerical effect without uncertainty can overstate precision.
revision: Report the confidence or credible interval, standard error, or another design-appropriate uncertainty measure.

name: Vague carrier noun
rationale: A carrier noun points backward without naming the result, making the claim portable across studies.
revision: Replace the vague noun with the specific exposure, outcome, estimate, subgroup, or mechanism.

name: Generic recommendation without actor and action
rationale: The recommendation provides no accountable actor, operational action, threshold, or setting.
revision: Specify the responsible actor, action, target population, timing, condition, and trade-off.

name: Interpretive claim without empirical or mechanistic anchor
rationale: The sentence interprets evidence but contains no estimate, source, mechanism, or named object that makes the interpretation testable.
revision: Attach the interpretation to the exact result or mechanism and state its limit.

name: Conclusion without empirical anchor
rationale: A conclusion that contains only significance language is detached from the study’s evidence.
revision: Carry forward at least one concrete result and one bounded implication.

name: Causal language–design mismatch
rationale: Causal verbs require an identification strategy, not only statistical adjustment.
revision: Use associational language or state the causal estimand, assumptions, design, and sensitivity analyses.

name: Unbounded generalization
rationale: Transport beyond the sampled population is asserted without a target population or effect-modifier assessment.
revision: Name the target population and justify transport using measured effect modifiers, sampling, or external evidence.

name: Statistical-to-clinical significance leap
rationale: A p-value does not establish clinical importance.
revision: Report absolute magnitude and compare it with a prespecified clinical threshold or decision model.

name: Mechanism claim without mediator evidence
rationale: A proposed mechanism should distinguish plausibility from measured mediation or intervention evidence.
revision: Label the mechanism as hypothesized unless mediator timing, confounding control, and pathway evidence support it.

name: Policy claim beyond the estimand
rationale: A study effect does not automatically identify the optimal policy.
revision: Separate the estimated contrast from implementation, costs, harms, feasibility, and distributional consequences.

name: Vague “standard methods” claim
rationale: A reproducibility claim replaces the details needed to reproduce the analysis.
revision: Name the model, estimand, variables, software/version, tuning or thresholds, missing-data handling, and uncertainty procedure.

name: Self-congratulatory method description
rationale: Method quality should be demonstrated by design and reporting, not asserted by praise adjectives.
revision: Delete the adjective and state the design feature that improves validity or reproducibility.

name: Method name-dropping without operational detail
rationale: Listing sophisticated methods without specifications creates an appearance of rigor without reproducibility.
revision: For each method, report the target quantity, inputs, assumptions, implementation choices, diagnostics, and uncertainty.

name: “Significant” without statistical support
rationale: The word significant is ambiguous unless statistical or practical significance is explicitly established.
revision: Report the estimate and interval; use “statistically significant” only with the criterion and “clinically important” only with a threshold.

name: “Trend” without magnitude or uncertainty
rationale: “Trend” can conceal a small, unstable, or non-monotonic estimate.
revision: Report the slope, contrast, time points, interval, and model used to test trend.

name: Interpretive language in Results
rationale: Explanations in Results can blur observation and interpretation, depending on journal style.
revision: Move causal or contextual interpretation to the Discussion unless the reporting format explicitly integrates them.

name: Percentage without denominator
rationale: A percentage without a denominator can hide sparse data or exclusions.
revision: Report n/N alongside the percentage at first mention and after subgroup changes.

name: Generic limitation theatre
rationale: Ritual caution is not a limitation analysis.
revision: Name the bias mechanism, likely direction, plausible magnitude, affected estimand, and whether any analysis addresses it.

name: Unsupported novelty claim
rationale: Priority and novelty claims require a defined comparison set and search boundary.
revision: Specify the dimension of novelty and the literature search or benchmark supporting it.

name: Importance claim without consequence
rationale: Importance is a relation to a decision, mechanism, or prior estimate, not an intrinsic adjective.
revision: State what decision changes, which prior belief is revised, or which mechanism becomes more plausible.

name: Citation laundry without synthesis
rationale: A sequence of study summaries can replace synthesis of agreement, heterogeneity, and bias.
revision: Compare studies on population, exposure, comparator, outcome, design, effect size, and likely bias.

name: Assistant-persona or prompt leakage
rationale: Interface language or model self-reference has leaked into the manuscript.
revision: Remove the leaked text and inspect adjacent passages for unreviewed generated content.

name: Citation placeholder
rationale: A placeholder may survive into submission and can conceal an unsupported claim.
revision: Insert and verify the source, or remove/qualify the claim.

name: Editorial placeholder or generation residue
rationale: Unresolved drafting residue indicates incomplete editorial control.
revision: Resolve the instruction, verify the surrounding content, and rerun the audit.

name: Numerical drift across sections
rationale: The same outcome or sample count can change between abstract, results, tables, and discussion.
revision: Link every headline number to a canonical result object and fail validation on unexplained divergence.

name: Terminology or estimand drift
rationale: Generated or heavily edited manuscripts may silently switch population, exposure, outcome, or effect measure labels.
revision: Define canonical terms and require section-level consistency or explicit distinction.

name: Cross-section claim contradiction
rationale: The abstract, results, and conclusion may make incompatible claims about direction or significance.
revision: Map claims to the same outcome and contrast, then resolve contradictory direction, magnitude, or certainty.
